info.title: Zeck Public API
info.summary: The execution-centric, provider-neutral public API surface of AI Execution OS.
info.description: Machine-readable contract of the public API transport surface. The ONE canonical wire source is src/shared/wire.ts (re-exported by sdk/index.ts); this document is a projection validated against the live route table by tests/unit/developer-docs/machine-schemas.test.ts. Core invariants: (1) Execution is THE primitive — there is no model-call or provider-call route; (2) provider/model identifiers cross only as opaque neutral strings inside route summaries; (3) no type carries secret material; (4) every scoped read/command carries the X-Zeck-Application header (creation carries applicationId in the body); (5) every POST requires an Idempotency-Key header; (6) unknown request keys are rejected fail-closed (closed contracts).

baseUrl.description: The deployment's public API base URL (developer-side variable ZECK_API_URL).

post.description: The frozen create contract (API-001): a task + constraints — provider selection is FORBIDDEN (unknown keys rejected fail-closed; the vocabulary provider/providerId/model/modelId/rail/connectionId/connection/agent/agentId must never appear). The application selector travels in the body's applicationId; the response is the durable ExecutionReceipt. Same Idempotency-Key + same request fingerprint replays the durable outcome (replayed=true); same key + different fingerprint returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

422.description: 422 — CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (a required capability is unavailable or the request is malformed) or NO_ELIGIBLE_ROUTE (no eligible execution route satisfied the task profile and constraints).

get.description: Policy-visible execution metadata only. Requires the X-Zeck-Application header; the effective tenant/application scope is derived server-side from durable membership rows. A scope-checked miss is 404 — another application's execution is indistinguishable from a missing one.

post.description: Cancellation goes THROUGH the execution lifecycle (the single write path): the authority validates the transition (non-terminal only) and appends the cancel envelope. Terminal executions return 409 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION.

get.description: The ordered, durable event ledger of the execution — lifecycle visibility, planning decisions, step facts. Payloads are scrubbed (secret-shaped keys redacted).

The result package computed ONLY from authority reads: route summary (from the ledger's planning decisions), settled cost/usage facts (or their honest null absence — never a fabricated number), output artifacts (id + digest), verification evidence and honest warnings.
The verification axis projection: every recorded criterion verdict with strategy, evaluator provenance, confidence and evidence references.

The governed inventory projection: agent summaries with lifecycle status and active version. There is NO agent mutation route on the public surface — agent identity, versions and promotions change through their owning authorities.
Agent summary + active version (with validation state) + latest promotion/rollback selection + all available versions.

post.description: A bounded, capability-gated payment INTENT provenance-bound to an execution. Proposing is NEVER an authorization — the governed admission chain (policy, capability, budget) decides server-side. The recipient is an opaque external reference; there is no field where a raw payment credential could even appear.

get.summary: Settlement and delivery as SEPARATE axes (scoped).
get.description: Payment success != resource delivered != execution success — a settlement alone never proves delivery. Settlements are correlated EXTERNAL observations (evidence only); deliveries are decided by the verification authority.

post.summary: Run an advisory codebase opportunity analysis (idempotent).
post.description: Analysis is an Execution: policy admission precedes codebase access; the analysis is bound to a governing execution and completes through verification (the analysis digest binding). The subgraph is pre-validated against the closed execution-graph contract — malformed selections fail closed with 422 and leave NO row anywhere. Findings are ADVISORY (advisory/candidate/verified — no 'promoted' state exists on this surface).

Preference-only answers over closed vocabularies — a rating is NEVER a verification PASS. The route DERIVES the finding/revision/context binding; the caller cannot assert it. Closed vocabularies: questionKind (pair-preference | behavior-preservation | replacement-acceptability), answer (prefer-candidate | prefer-baseline | no-difference | insufficient-information).

The single-step forward transition advisory -> candidate -> verified, gated on evidence (rating | verified-equivalence). No 'promoted' state exists on this surface — the promotion gate is external. Closed vocabularies: toState (advisory | candidate | verified), evidenceKind (rating | verified-equivalence).

get.description: Control-plane availability and dependency readiness are reported SEPARATELY. An authoritative dependency that is not ready makes the whole plane DOWN (503); non-authoristic dependencies degrade explicitly (200 with status 'degraded'). The response is scrubbed (secret-shaped keys and credential-shaped substrings never cross).

503.description: down (an authoritative dependency is not ready, or readiness is unattestable).

post.summary: Issue a scoped transport credential (show-once secret).
post.description: Creates a credential through the auth module's credential authority. The secret material is returned EXACTLY ONCE — on this response when replayed=false; a replay of the same Idempotency-Key returns the metadata-only record (secret=null). The idempotency ledger's durable outcome never contains secret material, so no later route, log or render path can retrieve it. The request body carries the application selector; the effective tenant/application scope is derived server-side from durable membership rows. Unknown keys are rejected fail-closed.

201.description: The durable issue outcome (show-once secret when this request created it).

422.description: 422 — CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (malformed request, or issuance is not enabled for this deployment / the authority is not wired in the composition).

get.description: Every credential visible to the request's application scope: identity, label, role/permission scope, creation/rotation timestamps and status. The response carries NO secret material and no secret reference (metadata-only by construction). The issuance.enabled fact states the deployment's issuance capability honestly.

post.description: Issues a successor secret under the SAME credential identity and retires the predecessor (status=retired, rotatedAt set, supersededBy naming the successor). The successor secret is shown EXACTLY ONCE on this response when replayed=false; a replay returns the successor record with secret=null. Revoked credentials cannot rotate (409 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION). Cross-tenant or cross-application targets fail TENANT_SCOPE_VIOLATION.

200.description: The successor record (show-once secret when this request executed the rotation).

422.description: 422 — CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (malformed request, or issuance is not enabled for this deployment).

post.description: Transitions the credential identity's current record to status=revoked — immediate and idempotent: revoking an already-revoked credential converges to the same durable outcome (no error). Rotation and revocation are both reflected in the list.

get.summary: List sandbox quota state for the caller's application scope

200.description: The per-dimension quota records (limit, consumption, window, status) with the honest telemetry boundary

get.summary: Read one disposable sandbox identity's honest expiration state

200.description: The identity record — post-expiry reads return the honest expired state, never a silent 404

404.description: No such identity visible to this scope

post.summary: Reset a disposable sandbox identity (idempotent, state-non-carrying)

200.description: The fresh successor identity; nothing carried forward; re-confirmation is a no-op success

404.description: No such identity visible to this scope

get.summary: The versioned synthetic-data policy artifact, served verbatim

200.description: The digest-carrying policy document (permitted/prohibited classes, enforcement points, violation-recording semantics)

get.description: The runtime deployment identity: the exact Git revision, the content-addressed deployment identity id, the manifest digest, the resource digest, the topology digest and the provider topology projection (concern, provider, authority role, substitution target, free-tier-first tier class). Hosting-independent by construction (no host/port/URL fields). An unbound composition answers the honest fail-closed 503 'unbound' state; verification recomputes everything against the current manifests (drift and tampering fail closed).

503.description: unbound or unattestable (the composition did not bind the deployment identity seam, or the seam failed).

bearerAuth.description: A Zeck transport credential (developer-side variable ZECK_TOKEN) — never a provider API key.

IdempotencyKey.name: idempotency-key
IdempotencyKey.description: Mandatory on every POST route. Same key + same request fingerprint replays the durable outcome; same key + different fingerprint returns 409.

ZeckApplication.name: x-zeck-application
ZeckApplication.description: The application-scope selector for every scoped read and governed command. The selector NAMES the application whose durable membership rows authorize the request; the effective scope is always derived server-side. A scoped request without it is rejected.

CredentialId.name: credentialId
CredentialId.description: The STABLE credential identity (shared across rotations; the list response names it).

AuthenticationFailed.description: 401 — missing or invalid bearer credential (not retryable).

AuthorizationDenied.description: 403 — the authenticated actor is not permitted this operation (not retryable).

PolicyDenied.description: 403 — the policy authority denied the operation (not retryable).

BudgetExceeded.description: 402 — a budget bound was exceeded (not retryable without a changed request).

IdempotencyKeyReused.description: 409 — the same key with a DIFFERENT request fingerprint (a client bug: surface it, never retry it).

CapabilityUnavailable.description: 422 — a required capability is unavailable, the request is malformed, or the scope-checked target is missing (404 mappings use this code with a 404 status).

NoEligibleRoute.description: 422 — no eligible execution route satisfied the task profile and constraints.

ProviderError.description: 502 — a provider-side failure (retryability follows the body's retryable field).

InvalidStateTransition.description: 409 — the lifecycle command is illegal for the current status (e.g. cancelling a terminal execution).

NotFound.description: 404 — the scope-checked target does not exist (indistinguishable from another application's target).

MicroUsd.description: Integer micro-USD (1e-6 USD) string — the platform money convention. Floats are never accepted.

ExecutionStatus.description: The execution lifecycle statuses. Terminal: COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED.

requestId.description: Correlation identifier for support (never internal host paths).

task.description: The customer task payload (e.g. {kind, doc, maxWords}). Provider selection is unrepresentable here.

userId.description: End user the execution (and any spend) is attributed to.

ExecutionRequest.description: The frozen create contract. The keys provider/providerId/model/modelId/rail/connectionId/connection/agent/agentId must NEVER appear — the server rejects them fail-closed and the SDK rejects them client-side.

replayed.description: True when the same idempotency key replayed a durable outcome.

RouteSummary.description: Opaque neutral strings — never SDK types, never provider selection inputs.

digest.description: Content digest (sha256 hex) when the platform recorded one.

executionId.description: The logical execution this economic action is provenance-bound to.

recipient.description: An opaque external recipient/seller reference (never a credential).

EconomicSettlement.description: A correlated EXTERNAL settlement observation (evidence only — never a Zeck money-movement truth source).

EconomicDelivery.description: Delivery EVIDENCE — the verification authority alone decides delivery.

subgraph.description: The selected execution-graph nodes (validated against the closed execution-graph contract before any side effect).

answer.description: The recorded answer (preference vocabulary — never a verification PASS).

eventId.description: Durable event identity (the receiver's dedupe key).

attempt.description: The delivery attempt number (1 = first attempt).

WebhookEvent.description: The signed webhook envelope (delivery surface, not an HTTP route): signed with HMAC-SHA256 hex over the canonical basis in the x-zeck-signature header; event id in x-zeck-event-id.

CredentialStatus.description: The credential lifecycle: active (usable), retired (superseded by a rotation successor), revoked (terminal; immediate and idempotent).

CredentialRecord.description: Metadata-only credential projection. NO field carries secret material or a secret reference — by construction there is no field where either could appear.

id.description: Row id of this record (one per issued secret binding).

credentialId.description: The STABLE credential identity — shared across rotations.

label.description: Operator-facing label (validated shape; never secret material).

role.description: The house role whose permission set scopes this credential.

rotatedAt.description: Set on the predecessor when its rotation successor was issued.

supersededBy.description: The successor record id after rotation (lineage fact).

permissions.description: The permission scope the authority derives from the role.

CredentialIssueRequest.description: The closed create contract: applicationId, label and role only — unknown keys are rejected fail-closed.

CredentialIssueResponse.description: Issue/rotate outcome. The show-once contract: secret is present ONLY when replayed is false (the request that durably created the credential); a replay of the same idempotency key returns the metadata-only record with secret=null, and no other route can retrieve it.

secret.description: Show-once secret material: present exactly once, on the response to the request that durably created it; null on every replay and every other route.

enabled.description: The deployment's issuance capability fact — false when the composition's secret store cannot hold issued credentials (the honest gate the console renders).
